stopped_because: ran the 5 iterations it was given
policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Apply the memory update from the observations before selecting the subgoal. Each episode starts with A: with the hand empty and remaining_targets nonempty, pick up the container corresponding to the first point in remaining_targets. For any A selection, match a visible container to the first remaining point only if its center is within 15 image-coordinate units of that point, or direct tracking evidence in the current execution frames establishes that it is the same container displaced from that location. Point inside the matched container. If no such match exists, treat the target as temporarily undetected and point at the remembered point. A recent detection near that point followed by disappearance does not justify switching to another container. When a completed pickup leaves a container held and another target remains, choose B to put down the container. A raised hand with fingers maintaining partial closure after grasp and lift is evidence of holding, even if object detections still report the old container center, provided no subsequent release is observed. When execution shows the fingers opening fully followed by hand retreat with the fingers remaining fully open, treat the release as complete and the hand as empty, even if an object detection still describes a container as lifted. This release evidence takes priority over conflicting object detections and the held-container fallback. With remaining_targets nonempty, choose A on the container corresponding to its first point; do not select the previously picked container again merely because it is still visible. Completion of the last requested pickup satisfies the goal, so no further command is needed unless another decision is requested. For an unexpected extra decision with no targets remaining, choose B as the available release action. For ambiguous or otherwise uncovered situations with remaining_targets nonempty, choose B if the observations indicate a held container and no subsequent release is observed; a lifted-container report alone cannot establish holding in the presence of an observed release. Otherwise choose A using the target-matching rule above; never substitute a distant visible container merely because it is the nearest detection to the first remaining point. Do not infer hidden cube colors from current container appearance.

fields.name: remaining_targets
fields.description: With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and use the demonstration to match each cube to the container placed over its location. Write the ordered list of those containers' centers as [y, x] points, excluding distractors. With existing memory, inspect the execution frames for a completed pickup of the first listed container: the hand approaches its location, closes to a nonzero grasp opening, and rises with the grasp maintained. On that observed completed pickup, remove the first entry exactly once. A static container detection at the old location does not negate the observed grasp-and-lift sequence. Do not remove an entry merely because you are now selecting A, because a container is already held without a new pickup, or because the hand releases a container. Preserve all other entries and their coordinates, including across put-down execution. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
